issues.sym: Misfires, a rough idle, stumbling or hesitation when you accelerate, vibration under load and a check engine light. It often gets worse in wet weather.
issues.why: The LT1 V8 uses an Optispark distributor mounted low on the front of the engine, right under the water pump. Its small vents let moisture build up inside, and a leaking water pump or road spray can soak it, which upsets the spark timing.
issues.next: Have the ignition system checked for misfire codes and look for coolant drips above the distributor. If the Optispark is bad, replace it with an improved vented unit and fix any water pump leak at the same time.

issues.t: Automatic transmission slipping or losing 3rd and 4th gear
issues.sym: The engine revs up without the car speeding up, especially on the shift into 3rd or 4th, or shifts get harsh, late or erratic. Eventually it may stop moving in some gears.
issues.why: The 4L60E automatic used behind both engines is a known weak point. Heat hardens the seal on the 3-4 clutch piston so pressure leaks and the 3-4 clutches burn out. A cracked sun shell can also take out gears.
issues.next: Check the fluid level and smell. Burnt-smelling or dark fluid is a bad sign. Avoid hard launches and have a transmission shop diagnose it early, since driving on a slipping transmission makes the rebuild bigger.

issues.t: Intake manifold gasket coolant leak (3.8L V6)
issues.sym: Coolant loss with no obvious puddle, coolant seeping where the intake meets the engine above the water pump, the engine running hot, or milky residue under the oil cap.
issues.why: The 3800 V6 is known for intake manifold gaskets that start leaking with age, sometimes into the engine and sometimes outside. Plastic coolant elbows on the intake are another weak spot.
issues.next: Don't ignore coolant loss. Coolant mixing into the oil can ruin the bearings. Have a shop pressure-test the cooling system and replace the intake gaskets and elbows if they are the source.

issues.sym: Coolant drips at the front of the engine, a sweet smell, the temperature gauge running high, or in bad cases white exhaust smoke and milky residue under the oil cap.
issues.why: The LT1 does not tolerate heat well. Water pump seal leaks and other cooling system failures let coolant run low, and running hot can blow a head gasket.
issues.next: Keep an eye on the coolant level and gauge. If it overheats, pull over and shut it off rather than driving on. Have the water pump and hoses pressure-tested before the head gaskets are damaged.

issues.sym: A light knocking or slapping sound for the first few minutes after a cold start that fades as the engine warms up. Some engines also use oil between changes, and worn ones may puff blue smoke at startup.
issues.why: Usually blamed on piston-to-cylinder clearance (often called piston slap) in the LS1 V8. Many engines make the noise and run for years.
issues.next: Check the oil level regularly and top up as needed. If the noise doesn't fade when warm, or oil use climbs, get a compression or leak-down test, since a real fix means taking the engine apart.

issues.t: Power windows slow down or stop working
issues.sym: One or both windows move slowly, struggle near the top, or quit working entirely. Some owners report motor failures at fairly low mileage.
issues.why: The factory window motors on these cars are weak and wear out, and the heavy frameless door glass makes them work hard.
issues.next: Have the motor tested at the door. Replacing the window motor is a fairly simple job. A window stuck down should be fixed soon to keep rain out.

issues.t: Pop-up headlight motor grinding or failing
issues.sym: A grinding noise when the headlights open or close, one headlight stuck up or down, or headlights popping up by themselves when you lock or unlock the car.
issues.why: The Firebird's pop-up headlights are raised by small electric motors with plastic gears that strip and break with age.
issues.next: Have the headlight motor and its gears checked. Rebuild kits and replacement motors are available, and a light stuck down is unsafe to drive with at night.

issues.t: Clutch release bearing noise and clutch wear (manual)
issues.sym: A grinding or whirring noise when you push the clutch pedal in, a pedal that feels soft, or gears that get hard to select.
issues.why: The clutch release (throwout) bearing wears out, and the factory clutch and clutch master cylinder on the 6-speed cars are not very durable, especially on modified cars.
issues.next: Have the clutch hydraulics checked. If the bearing is noisy, replace the clutch, release bearing and flywheel work together while the transmission is out to avoid paying labor twice.

issues.t: Rear axle wheel hop and weak 10-bolt rear end
issues.sym: The rear end shudders and hops on hard launches, and you may hear clunks or a whine from the rear axle over time.
issues.why: The 10-bolt rear axle is considered a weak point behind the V8, and the stamped steel lower control arms let the axle hop under hard acceleration, which strains the gears.
issues.next: Avoid hard launches. If the axle whines or clunks, have the gear oil and bearings checked. Upgraded control arm bushings or boxed arms reduce wheel hop.

issues.sym: A shaking steering wheel or pulsing brake pedal when you slow down, especially from highway speed.
issues.why: The factory front rotors on these cars warp easily with heat and hard use, and rotor complaints are the most common brake complaint filed with NHTSA for the 1999 model.
issues.next: Have the rotors measured. Replace pads and rotors as a set; many owners switch to better-quality aftermarket rotors and pads.

issues.sym: The temperature gauge climbs, especially in traffic or on hot days, and you may find brown sludge in the coolant reservoir.
issues.why: Sludge can build up and block the radiator when the long-life orange coolant is left low, mixed with other coolant, or not changed. Owners have linked radiator clogging on these cars to that coolant.
issues.next: Have the cooling system flushed and the radiator flow-checked. Keep the coolant topped up with the correct type and change it on schedule.

issues.sym: The engine won't crank or just clicks, the dash lights may flicker, and the security light flashes on the dash.
issues.why: The anti-theft system isn't recognizing the key. Worn key contacts or a failing ignition switch or lock cylinder can stop the system reading the key.
issues.next: Try a spare key. If the security light keeps flashing, have a shop or dealer check the ignition switch and key reading; replacing the ignition switch is a common fix.

issues.t: Misfires from oil-fouled plugs and worn plug wires (LT1)
issues.sym: Rough idle, jerking when you accelerate, hard starting and a loss of power, sometimes with a flashing check engine light.
issues.why: A clogged PCV valve lets oil mist get into the intake and coat the spark plugs, and Optispark trouble can damage the plug wires.
issues.next: Have the plugs pulled and inspected. Oil-covered plugs point to the PCV system, which should be cleaned or replaced along with the plugs and any damaged wires.

issues.sym: The low coolant light stays on even though the coolant is full and you can't find any leak.
issues.why: The coolant level sensor in the radiator is a common failure on the LT1. It only drives the dash light, so a bad sensor gives false warnings.
issues.next: First confirm the coolant really is full with the engine cold. If it is, the sensor is a simple part to replace.

issues.sym: Cracks in the top of the dashboard and in the interior trim near the windows, and cracked door panels.
issues.why: The interior plastics on the 1998-2002 cars break down with heat and age, and the door panels on these years are prone to cracking.
issues.next: This is cosmetic. Use a sunshade to slow the damage. Used or aftermarket replacement panels and dash covers are available.

issues.t: Clutch may not release when pedal is pressed (recall)
issues.sym: The car may keep pulling when you press the clutch, making it hard to shift, longer to stop, or causing the engine to stall.
issues.why: A small number of 1999 manual cars had a clutch part that could fail to disengage. GM recalled them (NHTSA 99V-239).
issues.next: Run your VIN through a recall lookup or ask a GM dealer whether the repair was done. It is free if it is still open.

issues.t: Seat belt retractors may not meet standards (recall)
issues.sym: You may not notice anything. The belt might not lock properly in a crash.
issues.why: Some 1997 Firebirds were built with seat belt retractors that may not meet the federal standard. GM recalled them (NHTSA 96V-219).
issues.next: Check your VIN for open recalls. If the repair was never done, a GM dealer will do it for free.

issues.t: Weak welds near the driver door hinge (recall)
issues.sym: Nothing obvious while driving. In a crash, the area near the door hinge may not hold as designed.
issues.why: Some 2002 Firebirds were built with welds near the door hinge area that may not meet crash standards. GM recalled them (NHTSA 01V-381).
issues.next: Check your VIN for open recalls and have a GM dealer do the free repair if it was never done.
